questions.text: In tennis, what is a score of zero called?
questions.explanation: 'Love' is the traditional tennis term for no points.

questions.text: What do golfers shout to warn people of a wayward ball?
questions.explanation: 'Fore' is the traditional warning cry on the course.

questions.text: On which surface is the Wimbledon tennis championship played?
questions.explanation: Wimbledon has always been played on grass.

questions.text: In golf, what is a score of one stroke under par on a hole called?
questions.explanation: Birdie is one under, eagle two under.

questions.text: How many holes are played in a standard round of golf?
questions.explanation: A full round on a standard course is 18 holes.

questions.text: Which city hosted the 1948 Summer Olympics, the first held after the Second World War?
questions.explanation: London staged the 1948 Games despite post-war austerity.

questions.text: Who was the first man to run a mile in under four minutes, in 1954?
questions.explanation: Bannister ran 3:59.4 at Oxford on 6 May 1954.

questions.text: Which major golf tournament is held each year at Augusta National and awards a green jacket?
questions.explanation: The Masters has been played at Augusta since 1934.

questions.text: On which surface is the French Open played?
questions.explanation: Roland Garros has red clay courts.

questions.text: A marathon is 26 miles and how many yards?
questions.explanation: The standard marathon distance is 26 miles 385 yards, or 42.195 km.

questions.text: Which player won all four tennis Grand Slam singles titles in the 1988 calendar year?
questions.explanation: Graf also won Olympic gold in 1988, completing a Golden Slam.

questions.text: Which golfer is nicknamed 'The Golden Bear'?
Which Australian won a calendar-year Grand Slam in both 1962 and 1969?
questions.explanation: Laver is the only man to have achieved the feat twice.

questions.text: Which Czech runner won the 5000m, 10,000m and marathon at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics?
questions.explanation: Zátopek's treble in Helsinki is legendary.

questions.text: Which Ethiopian won the 1960 Olympic marathon in Rome running barefoot?
questions.explanation: Bikila ran the course barefoot and set a world best.

spares.text: In tennis, what is a serve that the opponent cannot touch called?
spares.explanation: An ace wins the point outright.

spares.text: Which of the four tennis Grand Slam tournaments was first held in 1877?
spares.explanation: The first Wimbledon championship took place in 1877.

spares.text: In golf, what is a score of three strokes under par on a hole called?
spares.explanation: An albatross is also called a double eagle.

spares.text: Which Briton won the Olympic 1500m in both 1980 and 1984?
spares.explanation: Coe won in Moscow and Los Angeles.
